1	# Clerk — authentication for Next.js
2	
3	Clerk is a drop-in authentication and user management service. It ships React
4	components for sign-in and sign-up, session handling, and social login.
5	
6	## Install
7	
8	```bash
9	npm install @clerk/nextjs
10	```
11	
12	## 1. Environment variables
13	
14	```
15	NEXT_PUBLIC_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY=pk_test_placeholder
16	CLERK_SECRET_KEY=sk_test_placeholder
17	```
18	
19	## 2. Wrap the app
20	
21	`src/app/layout.tsx`:
22	
23	```tsx
24	import { ClerkProvider } from "@clerk/nextjs";
25	
26	export default function RootLayout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
27	  return (
28	    <ClerkProvider>
29	      <html lang="en"><body>{children}</body></html>
30	    </ClerkProvider>
31	  );
32	}
33	```
34	
35	## 3. Protect routes with middleware
36	
37	`src/middleware.ts`:
38	
39	```ts
40	import { clerkMiddleware, createRouteMatcher } from "@clerk/nextjs/server";
41	
42	const isProtected = createRouteMatcher(["/dashboard(.*)"]);
43	
44	export default clerkMiddleware(async (auth, req) => {
45	  if (isProtected(req)) await auth.protect();
46	});
47	
48	export const config = { matcher: ["/((?!_next|.*\\..*).*)", "/(api|trpc)(.*)"] };
49	```
50	
51	## 4. Sign-in and sign-up pages
52	
53	```tsx
54	import { SignIn } from "@clerk/nextjs";
55	export default function Page() { return <SignIn />; }
56	```
57	
58	Email + password and Google sign-in are both enabled from the Clerk dashboard;
59	no extra provider code is needed in the app.
60	
61	## 5. Read the current user on the server
62	
63	```ts
64	import { auth, currentUser } from "@clerk/nextjs/server";
65	
66	const { userId } = await auth();
67	const user = await currentUser(); // user.emailAddresses[0].emailAddress
68	```
69	
70	Use `userId` as the stable key when linking Clerk users to your own records.
71	
72	## Why teams pick Clerk
73	
74	- Sign-in, sign-up and account UI are prebuilt components, not code you maintain.
75	- Password hashing, sessions, and social providers are handled by the service.
76	- Free tier covers development and small production apps.

1. Create an app at [dashboard.clerk.com](https://dashboard.clerk.com) and copy `.env.example` to `.env.local`, filling in the real publishable/secret keys.
2. Under **User & authentication**, enable **Password** and **Email verification link** (magic link) as sign-in options, alongside the existing Google social connection.
3. Under user profile / account settings, enable **Allow users to delete their own account** so the `/account` page can offer account deletion.

## Develop

```bash
npm run dev
```

## Summary

Replaced the hand-rolled NextAuth + in-memory-user setup with **Clerk** (`@clerk/nextjs`) — it covers all three asks natively instead of requiring custom email/token infrastructure:

- **Magic-link sign-in**: `<SignIn>`/`<SignUp>` at `/signin`, `/signup` (Clerk catch-all routes) — Google, password, and email magic links all handled by Clerk once enabled in its dashboard, no app code per method.
- **`/account` page**: Clerk's `<UserProfile>` gives password change and account deletion out of the box; I added a custom "Devices" tab with a **sign out of all devices** action (a server action that revokes every active Clerk session for the user via the backend API, then redirects to `/signin`).
- **Auth checks**: moved from path-matching middleware to `auth.protect()` in each protected page (`/dashboard`, `/account`) — the middleware itself flagged `createRouteMatcher` as deprecated in the installed version and told me to do exactly this.
- Deleted `src/auth.ts`, `src/lib/users.ts`, the credentials/signup API route, and the old sign-in/sign-up pages.
- `.env.example` has placeholder Clerk keys plus notes on which dashboard toggles to flip (password + magic-link strategies, self-serve account deletion).
- Verified with `next build`, `eslint`, and an actual `next dev` run (well-formed placeholder key) — signed-out nav, redirects on protected routes, and page rendering all check out.

Worth knowing: this app's `@clerk/nextjs` came in at v7.9.1 — newer than what most docs/training data describe (`SignedIn`/`SignedOut`/`Protect` are gone, replaced by `<Show when="signed-in">`; `afterSignOutUrl` moved to `ClerkProvider`). I verified every API against the installed type declarations rather than assuming, so this should match what's actually in `node_modules`.

Not done: I didn't wire up real Clerk credentials or toggle the dashboard settings (password/magic-link/self-serve deletion) — that needs your actual Clerk account.
